description: Due to pollution, renewables like wind, solar, and hydro are vital, but limited solar power fails at night. Our idea uses moonlight, reflected sunlight, to boost solar efficiency and generate power after dark. This can help tackle energy shortages, promote sustainability, cut environmental impact, and advance universal electricity access for a safer planet.
summary: This project shows the transformation of Moon's resources. The energy can be obtained from sunlight and heat from regolith. Through solar energy collection during the day and heat energy generation at night using a Stirling generator, we developed an innovative idea to supply energy continuously. Furthermore, the task of having the lunar dust is solved by means of using piezo electric vibration to secure solar batteries. Lastly, the energy can be transferred to Earth with the help of microwave technologies. On the whole, Lunar Vision offers a new way of utilizing resources from the Moon.
details:
Lunar Vision is an innovative energy solution that aims to tackle the challenge of supplying electricity during the very long lunar night. Given that there are around 14 Earth days of lunar time when the Moon remains in darkness, solar panels cannot work on their own to produce power.

The project can be characterized as an energy system that works on the principle of integration of several different technologies. Photovoltaic panels generate electricity from sunlight during the lunar day. Moreover, part of the produced thermal energy can be stored with the help of lunar regolith, the natural material that covers the Moon's surface. The stored heat can finally be used to operate the Stirling generator, which transforms thermal energy into mechanical energy and electricity.

Microwave wireless power transmission is another proposed element. This process converts energy via microwaves from one place to another. The entrepreneur must have a rectenna, which is a transmission system with a receiving antenna. The rectenna can convert microwave energy into electricity, but long-distance transfer of energy shows some difficulties, such as energy losses, difficulty with transmission efficiency and beam alignment.

Lunar Vision is also looking at piezoelectric technology in order to reduce the accumulation of lunar dust on solar panels. Lunar dust may affect energy collection efficiency; therefore, it is crucial to remove dust for operations on the Moon.

Even though its design is full of promise, the project needs proper testing. This will necessarily entail a host of measurements starting with the evaluation of the thermal energy of the regolith, thereby estimating the electrical output of the Stirling generator, and finally measuring the efficiency of microwave transmission. Moreover, all parts must also go through compatibility tests.

To summarize, Lunar Vision applies certain known scientific principles in an attempt to create a solution for sustainable lunar energy. Although it still faces a series of technical problems, the project already serves as a starting point on the way to more reliable energy systems for lunar operations in the future
